analysis:
Examined the four changed files.

StartCommand+ClusterMember.swift (head 15-16, 62, 95-96): adds an answersUpdateDrain flag, default false. It is forwarded to ProviderLoopConfig.clusterMemberAnswersUpdateDrain, and runClusterMember sets it true. The drain-handling implementation in ProviderLoop is not supplied. Integration should confirm that the drain only stops admission or finishes accepted work. It must not bypass the App Attest or pair authorization from TB-011/T-053 or change cancellation semantics (T-010).

UpdateCommand.swift (head 107-108, 117-118, 179-234): when no LaunchAgent is loaded but ClusterService.running(), update writes a ClusterPairUpdate.Request to the service directory. That directory is derived from ClusterService.paths().lock's parent. The command then polls the progress file until the drain timeout.
- The update itself still goes through SelfUpdater, so hash and quarantine checks are unchanged.
- The request file is a local control channel to the supervisor running as the same UID, similar to the local channels in TB-012/T-060. Any same-UID process could forge a request or progress record. The impact appears limited to a restart or drain (availability, A-018), which the operator can already cause. It grants no trust.
- Not visible: the writeRequest/readProgress implementations (file permissions, no-follow handling, bounded reads) and how the supervisor validates a request and the --version check. Without them, a parsing or symlink weakness cannot be ruled out.

main.swift: comment-only change. It notes that the supervisor compares --version output exactly (ClusterCandidateRecovery.startCheckFailure). A version string is not an integrity proof (T-013/T-034). If the supervisor treats a matching version as authorization to run a candidate binary, that needs review, but its source is not supplied.

OnboardingChecks.swift: test-only additions for oneBuild.

No concrete regression is visible in the supplied lines. Deeper review is needed of ClusterPairUpdate file IO, the supervisor's restart path (rollback per T-043) and the ProviderLoop update-drain handling.
